mechanism_narrative: The sharp drop in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES signals fewer in-person trips into central shopping areas, which should continue to depress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. If commuting remains suppressed, retail footfall falls further than the recent 4-week average.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -18.1 to -24.3 and WORKPLACES from -5.6 to -20.6 over the snapshot window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline below its last-4-weeks mean even though TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain at or below the current snapshot levels for the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while TRANSIT remains deeply negative, more time is spent near home and fewer discretionary shopping trips occur, pushing RETAIL_REC lower within two weeks. The effect is strongest when residential mobility rises in parallel with commuting suppression.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL above 15 and TRANSIT below -20 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose to 16.4 while TRANSIT fell to -24.3 in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days despite RESIDENTIAL staying above 15 and TRANSIT staying below -20.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in PARKS use indicates warmer-weather leisure substitution that diverts time and spending away from indoor retail, so RETAIL_REC should weaken over the next four weeks when park activity is still recovering. The signal fails if park mobility rebounds without a further retail decline.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -20.1 to -14.7 across the snapshot but remains below baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases relative to its last-4-weeks mean while PARKS remains at or above -15 for the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES falls below -15 after a prior week above -10, it marks a fresh tightening of on-site activity or renewed caution, and retail visits should drop with a one-week lag. The effect should appear quickly and be visible in the next week, not only after a month.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES crosses from above -10 to below -15 week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES moved from -10.6 to -20.6 in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the week after WORKPLACES crosses below -15 from above -10.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in GROCERY_PHARM alongside weak RETAIL_REC implies essential trips are absorbing shopping demand without restoring discretionary retail, so retail remains below its prior 4-week average over the next two weeks. This mechanism is falsified if grocery activity rises but retail also rises immediately.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM increased from 6.0 to 10.6 while RETAIL_REC declined from -13.4 to -15.0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC moves above its last-4-weeks mean within 14 days while GROCERY_PHARM remains elevated.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in GROCERY_PHARM with simultaneous RESIDENTIAL growth implies more local errand clustering and fewer long discretionary shopping trips, which should lift RETAIL_REC modestly over four weeks as nearby shopping consolidates. The claim fails if higher home-centered activity does not translate into retail trips.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL above 13 and GROCERY_PHARM above 8 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose to 10.6 and RESIDENTIAL to 16.4 in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays at or below its last-4-weeks mean over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL > 13 and GROCERY_PHARM > 8.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT remains below -20 for two consecutive weeks, the city is still operating under a low-mobility regime that suppresses destination retail traffic, so RETAIL_REC should stay negative over the next month. The effect is conditioned on continued low transit access, not on retail-specific shocks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -20 for 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was -19.9 in t-1w and -24.3 in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-weeks mean even though TRANSIT remains below -20 for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in PARKS and RESIDENTIAL indicates a home-and-local-leisure pattern that substitutes away from shopping districts; when both increase together, RETAIL_REC should underperform within two weeks. The mechanism is weakest if park visits rise without any extra time spent at home.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 3 points while RESIDENTIAL rises by at least 2 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -18.1 to -14.7 while RESIDENTIAL rose from 13.0 to 16.4
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days despite simultaneous week-on-week gains in PARKS and RESIDENTIAL.
